one_liner: Contracts manager and management analyst for a Marine Corps information operations center, running acquisition packages, overseeing contracts as COR, and advising leadership on resources.
fit_summary: This GS-13 role requires a year of GS-12-equivalent experience in acquisition and procurement support, organizational process analysis, and resource advising. Daniel's IEM consulting background may touch government contracts, but nothing on file shows hands-on PWS, IGCE, COR, or procurement work at that level. The SCI clearance requirement adds another hurdle.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status needed.

At least one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12 in all three areas: improving organizational structures and processes, advising leadership on financial, manpower and material resources, and technical support for acquisition and procurement activities.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance, which requires a Top Secret-level investigation.
You must pass the USA Hire assessment cut score; skipping it or scoring below it disqualifies you.
strategy: Before investing time, list honestly what you did at IEM involving government contracts: proposals, task orders, deliverables tracking, client funding, or process improvement. If none of it touches acquisition, apply to GS-9/11 management or program analyst roles instead.

If you did support contract work, frame it from the government side. Describe managing deliverables against a statement of work, tracking contract funding, writing cost estimates, and briefing client leadership on resources.
Map each of the three specialized-experience elements to a short, dated bullet on a two-page resume. Include start and end dates, hours per week, and the posting's exact terms.
The posting window is October 29 to November 2, 2026, only about five days. Have your two-page resume ready in advance, and finish USA Hire right away when the link arrives.
Answer the assessment truthfully. Overclaiming 'expert' acquisition experience you can't document in the resume can be caught in the Structured Resume Review.
resume_bullets: Managed [number] deliverables under a [client agency] contract valued at [$ amount], tracking performance against the statement of work and resolving issues with client stakeholders.
Analyzed [client/program] processes and recommended [specific change] to leadership, improving [metric] by [result].
Drafted [cost estimates/market research/scopes of work] supporting [type of procurement] for [government client], coordinating with [contracting staff/program leads].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would build an acquisition package, including PWS, IGCE and QASP, for a new services requirement.
Describe a time a contractor was underperforming. How did you document it and drive corrective action?
How have you advised leadership on reallocating funds, staff or materials to meet mission priorities?
Tell us about a time you improved an organizational process or procedure. What was the measurable result?
watch_outs: The application window is extremely short, about five days.
An SCI clearance is required. The investigation is lengthy, and the offer may be contingent on it.
The acquisition specialty is a hard requirement. Without demonstrable COR or procurement experience at the GS-12 level, you will likely be rated ineligible.
Veterans' preference applies under category rating, so preference-eligible applicants are listed first within each category.
